en.t: Unless and when for the future
en.g: Use unless, when, as soon as and before to talk about the future.
p: After when, as soon as, before and unless, use the present: When I get home, I'll call you.
Unless means if not: I'll go unless it rains = I'll go if it doesn't rain.
When is sure, if is possible: When I see Ana (I will) vs If I see Ana (maybe).
en.q: What's the first thing you'll do as soon as you get home today?
en.c: Write four sentences about tomorrow, one each with when, as soon as, before and unless.

Unless heißt wenn nicht: I'll go unless it rains = I'll go if it doesn't rain.

en.t: Writing a postcard or travel post
en.g: Describe a trip in a few friendly lines.
p: Mix tenses: The weather is lovely. We've seen the old town. Tomorrow we're going to the lake.
Add feelings and details: The food is amazing. The people are really friendly.
Friendly opening and ending: Hi everyone! / Wish you were here! / See you soon.
en.q: If you posted about your favourite trip, what three things would you mention?
en.c: Write a five-line postcard or travel post: the weather, what you've done and tomorrow's plan.

de.t: Eine Postkarte oder einen Reisepost schreiben

Gefühle und Details: The food is amazing. The people are really friendly.
Anfang und Schluss: Hi everyone! / Wish you were here! / See you soon.

fr.q: Si tu publiais un post sur ton voyage préféré, quelles trois choses mentionnerais-tu ?

en.g: Join two sentences with who, which and that.
p: Who for people: She's the teacher who helped me. Which for things: the bus which goes to town.
That works for both in everyday speech: the man that called, the film that won.
Don't repeat the subject: the book which is on the table, not the book which it is on the table.
en.q: Can you describe your favourite person and favourite object using who and which?

en.t: Where and whose in relative clauses
en.g: Add details about places and owners with where and whose.
p: Where for places: That's the café where we met. This is the town where I grew up.
Whose for possession: I have a friend whose dog is huge. (= her dog is huge)
Whose replaces his, her or their: the boy whose bike was stolen, not the boy who his bike.
en.q: Tell me about a place where something important happened to you.
en.c: Write three sentences with where about places you love and three with whose about people.

Whose ersetzt his, her, their: the boy whose bike was stolen, nicht the boy who his bike.

en.g: Talk around a word you don't know so people still understand.
